children: New Delhi, Nov. 3 -- Tamilnadu Petroproducts shares jumped 7% on Tuesday, 3 November, following the announcement of its Q2 FY27 results, which showed strong year-on-year growth in revenue and profitability.

The company's consolidated revenue from operations more than doubled, rising 104.9% year-on-year to Rs.934.37 crore in the September quarter, compared with Rs.456.09 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.

The firm's consolidated Profit before tax (PBT) increased 94.4% to Rs.87.86 crore from Rs.45.19 crore a year ago. Profit after tax (PAT) grew 89.9% to Rs.65.03 crore, against Rs.34.24 crore in Q2 FY26.
For the first half of FY27, consolidated revenue from operations surged 86.3% year-on-year to Rs.1,712.29 crore, compared with Rs.918.92 crore in the year-ago period.
Consolidated PBT more than doubled, increasing 109.5% to Rs.193.93 crore from Rs.92.56 crore. Consolidated PAT also more than doubled, rising 108.9% to Rs.145.14 crore from Rs.69.49 crore in H1 FY26.

Commenting on the performance, Ashwin Muthiah, Vice Chairman of Tamilnadu Petroproducts Ltd and Founder Chairman of AM International, Singapore, said the company delivered a strong quarter, with revenue and profitability more than doubling over the corresponding period last year.

He attributed the performance to the company's ability to navigate a challenging macroeconomic environment through operational improvements, cost discipline and a sharper focus on customer requirements.

Muthiah added that sustainable products and carbon-neutral manufacturing would remain central to the company's long-term growth strategy as it works towards building a more competitive and future-ready business.

Tamilnadu Petroproducts share price today opened at Rs.122.60 apiece on the BSE, the stock touched an intraday high of Rs.129.10 per share, and an intraday low of Rs.115.90 per share. The stock has jumped 37% so far in 2026.

Gaurav Arora, Head of Research at SAHI, said Tamilnadu Petroproducts has been in a downward trajectory since hitting a high of around Rs.147 and is currently trading within a parallel channel. The stock has made several attempts to move higher but has faced selling pressure at successive highs.

In Tuesday's session, the stock attempted to break above Rs.122 but formed a long upper wick, indicating selling pressure at higher levels. Arora said Rs.118 is the immediate support, while a break below this level could take the stock towards the next support at Rs.112.50.

He added that volatility has increased following the Q2 results. However, the technical structure is likely to remain range-bound with a cautious bias until the stock manages a convincing close above Rs.122.
